title: Use one steering-input acquisition path for ready and delivering reads
evidence: ready.rs:87-377 and delivering_steering.rs:81-388 acquire the same input, leaf, gate, generation, route head, binding head, binding, snapshot and active-CAS-turn closure, then recheck mutable anchors; each maintains an almost identical family of early-missing/drift helpers.

accepted_delivery/validation.rs:68-127 and delivering_steering/validation.rs:61-120 repeat the same execution relationship predicate. Their route predicates differ in eligible lifecycle and aggregate counter.
delivering_steering_read.rs:328-390 requires exactly twelve point reads even for a 384-member generation. Existing ready and delivering metrics must keep identifying their public operation.
proposal: Introduce a private SteeringReadKind enum and one acquired steering view. Keep thin public wrappers returning their existing types. Parameterize eligibility, route counter, operation-specific diagnostics and metrics; share acquisition, anchor confirmations and the exact execution predicate. Keep ready non-Routed input as stabilized absence while delivering non-Routed remains an anchor-confirmed invariant. Do not broaden the closure or scan generation membership.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve all public result types, error categories/operation names, constituent point limits, two-read mutable anchors, loaded generation and timestamp checks. Internal helper names/types may change.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Deduplicate acquisition and anchor helpers plus one ~60-line execution predicate; reserve 70-110 lines for the kind policy, shared view, wrappers and regression adjustments. Excludes the independent test-fixture loop removal SQ-006.

verification: Run existing ready/delivering eligibility, missing-record, corruption and drift cases with test-faults.
Keep exactly twelve eligible-path point reads and bounded behavior for large generations; compare metrics separately for both APIs.
Add only missing lifecycle asymmetry cases if existing tests do not cover non-Routed ready versus delivering and per-anchor mutation timing.

title: Share bounded encoded-content range filling
evidence: marker.rs:81-179 and provider.rs:239-360 both locate a ContentByteSpans predecessor and continue forwards while filling a bounded destination; each separately loads/checks chunks and slices offsets.
validation/content/range.rs:145-246 repeats the same encoded-range transport into a Vec and is reused for marker validation and provider completion/source checks.

The caller contracts differ: marker output is exactly 25 bytes, public provider output carries accounting and independently validates spans/chunks, while validation ranges reject zero length and cap each returned range at 65,536 bytes.
proposal: Implement one concrete encoded-content fill algorithm over a caller-supplied bounded output slice, with small store/DomainReader read adapters and a one-chunk cache. Return separate index/chunk accounting so wrappers preserve current public stored/decoded byte semantics. Keep each wrapper's range/frontier validation and diagnostics. Let the validation Vec wrapper allocate only the already bounded requested length. Share byte transport, not the narrative-generation/chain or marker semantic proof.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve marker tag/ID/label bytes and SHA-256, physical chunk identity/digest/length and span-key checks, gap detection, fixed page/point bounds, typed ReadError provenance, provider source frontier and terminal chain checks. Arbitrary encoded byte windows must not be replaced by UTF8-clipping text pages.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Replace three copies of predecessor/forward/chunk slicing mechanics; reserve 100-160 lines for shared fill and two transport/accounting adapters. Excludes logical text frontend SQ-003 and provider structural narrative append SQ-004.

verification: Run sealed content/segment range tests including forged marker bytes, changed boundary, missing chunk, UTF8 clipping and exact accounting.
Run provider narrative/completion range tests for crossing span/chunk/page boundaries, first mismatch, stale source, gaps and final chain.
Verify maximum payload/cached-chunk residency and preserve no whole-content allocation.

title: Share sealed text page orchestration for whole content and proven segments
evidence: content_text.rs:143-219 and segment.rs:261-347 repeat input ceiling checks, stabilized manifest absence, manifest validation, empty-page assembly, desired end calculation, existing read_text_page invocation, second manifest equality, UTF8 boxing and residency release.
They already share read_text_page and MarkerPolicy, so an additional private page orchestrator removes actual duplication without inventing a general streaming framework.
Whole-content offset validation occurs after manifest acquisition; segment offset validation occurs before it. Marker-free and proven-segment physical boundary semantics must stay distinct.
proposal: Use a private content/segment request enum to drive shared manifest-stabilized assembly and a common internal text-page result; retain each public wrapper and its validation order, operation diagnostics and segment fields. Eliminate the second pure validate_manifest after second==first proves the previously validated manifest unchanged. Keep proof acquisition separate from page reading.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve marker rejection versus opaque segment authorization, offset error variants/order, terminal empty page, exact continuation, zero-copy into_text behavior, independent page-time marker boundary checking and test-fault residency drop timing.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Deduplicate the ~75-line orchestration bodies while retaining request-specific validation and result wrappers; reserve helper/policy/regression glue. No byte transport savings counted here.

verification: Run content_text_range and content_text_segment_range with fault features, especially missing/reference mismatch precedence, nonprogress UTF8, leading/adjacent/trailing empty segments.
Retain manifest-change concurrent error, zero-copy pointer assertion and bounded later-page reads after a large proof scan.
Retain lifecycle residency tests through both tracked production paths.

Keep staged/published completion handling, source-byte availability and generation seed checks in their current callers. Retain exact key/value validation in the shared helper and allow operation-specific diagnostics where tests require them.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Remove one ~55-line duplicate append block, reserve helper signature/policy glue and small verification adjustments. Error adapter removal belongs only to SQ-005.

verification: Run staged provider frame, published source replay, narrative prefix and completion validation cases.
Exercise changed key/value, frame digest, source offsets, wrong chain, multiple completion spans and partial staging.
Retain physical ReadError classification.

Seven helpers/inline matches in completion, prefix, published, source, physical and projection source merely translate those variants losslessly.

Only two mutation callers use ProviderFrameStorageValidationError (mutation/provider_frame/completion.rs:108-111 and mutation/live/event/item/publication.rs:39-40); their Read versus domain-specific mutation failure distinction must remain as explicit boundary maps.
proposal: Use the existing crate-private SyndicValidationError throughout provider storage and span validation, including the text-span sink associated Error. Remove both duplicate internal enums and lossless conversion helpers. Update the two mutation boundary imports/patterns while preserving their domain-specific mappings. Keep the FrameChunkReader ReadError side channel required to cross std::io unchanged; do not parse Display/source chains.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Delete two small enums and lossless internal mapping bodies/calls, subtract import and two caller boundary adjustments. Excludes root-wide manual Error/Display derive opportunities and SQ-004 append sharing.

verification: Run provider staging/completion/source replay and schema validation corruption tests.
Verify physical failures still become DomainCallbackSource::Read and mutation physical Read variants; invariant failures retain typed domain rejection.
Check default and test-faults builds for sink generic constraints and updated internal exports.

Seven rewrites are exact identities. The HistorySummary arm advances revision a second time; preserve that final revision by constructing it directly at line 92.

title: Share revision-fenced accepted-source page transport
evidence: Both ~90-line modules construct the same global ThreadRouteKey bounds, validate a revision-bearing cursor, clamp limits, read one forward page, validate identity, recheck domain revision and construct a continuation.
AcceptedNext wraps each record in AcceptedNextSource with source_revision, while ready returns the record. Public cursors and stale/invalid diagnostics deliberately differ.
proposal: Introduce a private ThreadRouteKey source-page transport specialized through two small family/record adapters. It should return bounded records, accounting and last key after revision confirmation. Keep public cursors/types and their validation in thin wrappers; avoid extending this into a general query framework.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve domain revision fence before and after every page, strict cursor identity, per-API clamped maxima and next-source revision wrapper.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Deduplicate ~70 lines of transport and metadata logic after retaining two cursor/result wrappers and minimal family identity adapters.

verification: Run accepted ready/next source-page continuation, stale source, invalid cursor and key/value mismatch cases.
Retain empty-page-with-has_more invariant and exact stored/decoded accounting.

title: Retain exhaustive corruption validation and historical descendant boundaries
evidence: Explicit validation must visit malformed physical records outside typed ranges and orphan reverse indexes; recovery_reads exercises 63 families x three malformed encodings.
Historical context, binding, promotion, compaction and transcript witnesses intentionally permit selected-away paths and allowed descendant revisions.
Provider/item replay already reuses canonical parser/materialization logic and streams compact state. Draft marker admission membership is explicitly bounded by its admitted tree envelope.
proposal: Reject replacing exhaustive validators with ordinary bounded read methods, sampling, only forward-reference checks, current-record equality, or whole-home collections. Reject generic ORM/serde/state-machine dependencies for these exact V7 key/tag and provenance contracts. Local pure predicates may be shared only after identifying an identical relationship and retaining context-specific acquisition and temporal rules.
required_contract_changes: Those rejected alternatives would weaken physical corruption coverage, exact durable provenance or historical lifecycle semantics; no such contract change is recommended.
verification: Keep exhaustive malformed physical record matrix and explicit schema-validation versus routine reopen distinction.
Keep selected-away context, old projection generation, prefix replay and frontier corruption tests.

title: Defer broader recovery/stop consolidation and cross-slice expected-record reuse
evidence: Stop admission contains overlapping recovery facts and stop observations, but its raw-pass versus complete-pass confirmation schedule is exercised by mutation at the eighth and thirty-third read.
Several immutable target tuples recur in recovery and validation; current-gate revision constraints and binding kinds differ.
Promotion successor derivation and activity/assistant phase folds may duplicate mutation-owned code, but caller body ownership lies in another audit slice.
proposal: Do not assign savings for a broad unified recovery snapshot or wholesale validator merge without a concrete race-preserving design. Coordinate pure expected-record/phase/order helper opportunities with the mutation reviewer and count them once there if confirmed. Retain option fields needed to represent independently missing corrupt constituents.
required_contract_changes: None proposed. Any changed corruption-versus-drift result or observation boundary would require explicit authority review.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Deferred/coordination opportunity, no speculative or double-counted savings.

verification: If later pursued, preserve all stop-admission fault races, missing/reverse authority cases and typed ineligibility states.
Trace pure constructors across mutation and reconciliation before estimating deletion.
